minutes.headline: Select Board heard a cannabis dispensary pitch, deferred the trash-bag fee vote, and extended two contracts.
minutes.summary: The board appointed a new assessor, then heard a cannabis retail pitch for 43 Summer Street that stalled on a dispute over whether a neighboring house is a residential use. The town manager reported that public safety carport bids and the Flat Hill culvert estimate came in well above plan. The board extended two contracts, deferred the pay-as-you-throw bag fee vote to the next meeting, and went into executive session.

what_happened.line: The board voted to extend the town manager and director of municipal finance contract terms to July 31, 2021, with no one opposed.
The board put off the vote on the pay-as-you-throw bag fee increase and a senior bag pilot until its next meeting.
The town manager recommended against building the public safety carport at the bid price, and reported a higher revised estimate for the Flat Hill culvert.
An applicant presented an adult-use cannabis dispensary for 43 Summer Street; it was told to send a draft host community agreement to the town manager.
The board appointed Christine Cosgrove to the board of assessors until the next annual town election, by voice vote with no one opposed.

why_it_matters: The bag fee vote and the senior bag pilot bear on what households pay to throw out trash, and the vote is still ahead.
The carport and culvert estimates rose past plan, so those projects may need new funding decisions or be dropped.
A cannabis host community agreement would decide whether the town takes in sales revenue, and where a retail store sits next to homes.
watch_next: The next Select Board meeting, where the pay-as-you-throw bag fee increase and senior bag pilot are due for a vote.
The draft host community agreement for 43 Summer Street, which the applicant is to send to the town manager.
